interest: This document highlights the geopolitical interest surrounding diplomatic and naval contacts between the Empire of Japan and the Ethiopian Empire immediately prior to the outbreak of the Second Italo-Ethiopian War. The reception of Japanese naval vessels at Djibouti by an official Ethiopian delegation in mid-1934 reflects growing bilateral ties between Addis Ababa and Tokyo, an alignment that alarmed European colonial powers (especially Italy) and was closely monitored by American diplomats in the region.
overview: This file consists of a single-page Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet under decimal file 894.3351V, concerning visits of Japanese naval vessels and aircraft to ports of the French Somali Coast (French Somaliland). The lone entry records a cross-reference to Despatch No. 17 of August 24, 1935, from Cornelius Van H. Engert in Ethiopia, reporting on the June 1934 visit to Djibouti of two Japanese naval vessels (rendered as the gunboats 'ACAMA' and 'IZATA', likely the armored cruisers Asama and Iwate), where they were formally received by an official Ethiopian delegation, cross-referenced to file 784.94/23.

subfiles.about: A Department of State list of papers recording a cross-reference to a report on Japanese naval vessels visiting Djibouti in French Somaliland.
subfiles.summary: This single-page Department of State docket sheet indexes records categorized under decimal file 894.3351V regarding Japanese naval visits to the French Somali Coast. It documents an entry from Despatch No. 17 dated August 24, 1935, sent by Cornelius Van H. Engert from Ethiopia. The entry notes the June 1934 visit to Djibouti of two Japanese warships—noted in the purport as the gunboats 'ACAMA' and 'IZATA'—and mentions their reception by an official Ethiopian delegation, directing researchers to decimal file 784.94/23 for the underlying correspondence.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Visits of Japanese Naval Vessels to French Somali Coast
